answer: A Sybil-resistance mechanism is the beacon-priced entry bond: each epoch a public beacon samples a random delay and price, and every new identity must lock that price as a bond releasable only after the sampled delay. The price tracks the cohort tide, rising when registrations spike, so an attacker minting fifty fake identities pays fifty frozen, unproductive bonds. A canyon-shaped fee curve makes later registrants pay steeply more, so mass splitting cannot be timed cheaply. Honest users recover the bond at maturity; colluders face slashing, making fake votes costlier than any reward.
